title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 44
paragraphs: When Xerxes had come to the middle of Abydos, he desired to review the whole army. A raised seat of white stone had been prepared for him beforehand on a hill at this place, built by the people of Abydos on the king's previous command. There he took his seat, and looking down upon the shore he surveyed both the land army and the ships. As he gazed at them, the wish came over him to see a regatta held among the ships. When it took place and the Sidonian Phoenicians were victorious, he was delighted both with the race and with the whole armament.
